content:
maria: FYI after the overnight kernel+driver roll to a100-gw hosts, we've got a regression: peer-to-peer disabled on a subset of GPUs. Observed perf regression on short-seq workloads (~15-35%). 
deploy-bot: deploy event 1765129800: kernel-6.1.z + nvidia-driver-532.xx rolled to eu-west canary -> batch
alex: On affected node `a100-r3n12` `nvidia-smi topo -m` shows GPUs not grouped for P2P. `cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer` returning 0 for many pairs.
sam: I pulled lspci on a couple hosts: BAR1 ranges look smaller than expected (reported 256M on bad hosts vs 4G on healthy ones). PCIe ACS present but peer access blocked.
josh: Repro steps I used locally:
```bash
# quick peer test
nvcc --version || true
python - <<'PY'
from numba import cuda
for i in range(cuda.get_num_devices()):
    for j in range(cuda.get_num_devices()):
        if i!=j:
            print(i,j,cuda.current_context().device.can_access_peer(j))
PY
```
Results: several pair checks false on affected machines.
lia: Which racks/regions? Any correlation with BIOS versions?
maria: Mostly r3 and r7 in eu-west; two hosts in us-west-2. Non-affected machines running newer BIOS microcode.
alex: Quick mitigation that worked on a canary: added kernel cmdline `pcie_acs_override=downstream` and rebooted -> P2P restored and NCCL perf returned to baseline for microbench. Note: that weakens PCIe isolation (security tradeoff).
sam: Another short-term: rolling back to previous kernel+driver also restores P2P. We've started rollbacks on the batch where canary failed.
josh: nv_peer_mem/nvlink modules didn't fix behavior; this looks like a BAR assignment/ACPI/kernel change that reduces BAR1 aperture so driver disables peer mappings.
infra-bot: action INFRA-1234 created: "a100 peeraccess regression detection & gate" assigned to eng-infra
maria: Immediate plan:
- Alex: complete rollbacks for remaining hosts in the eu-west batch (doing now).
- Lia: pause any cross-region rollouts until triage complete.
- Josh: run automated P2P check and NCCL microbench on rolled-back vs still-affected hosts.
- Sam: open firmware/BIOS support ticket with vendor, include lspci/dmesg/cmdline samples.
- Infra: add a pre-rollout P2P health gate to the pipeline.
alex: I've started collecting artifacts: `dmesg | grep -i pcie`, full `lspci -vvv`, `nvidia-smi topo -m`, kernel cmdline for 8 affected + 8 unaffected hosts. Attaching to INFRA-1234.
sam: Hypothesis chain:
1) kernel change altered BAR allocation behavior or ACPI hint interpretation.
2) BAR1 small -> driver refuses to map peer BAR regions -> peer access disabled.
3) NCCL falls back to host-paths -> throughput/latency regression.
We need triage across kernel, driver, firmware.
lia: Notifying support and impacted Dedicated customers now. Will mark clusters in console with "degraded-inference-p2p" tag.
maria: Can infra healthcheck emit a severity numeric? e.g. percent GPUs failing P2P -> trigger page if >10%?
infra-bot: healthcheck feature request created.
josh: Alternatives if rollback is operationally heavy:
- Push grub change `pcie_acs_override=downstream` to affected nodes prior to reboot (fast but security tradeoff).
- Use per-host firmware update to ensure BAR windows allocated correctly (medium term).
- Gate all future kernel/driver rollouts with a small microbench canary plus P2P matrix check (long term).
alex: One strange host where ACS shows enabled but peers still blocked; collecting strace/dmesg, may be a BIOS bug around PCIe upstream bridges.
maria: After rollbacks finish, collect sample artifacts from 10 bad + 10 good nodes and attach to vendor ticket. Lia will coordinate customer comms.
lia: Update: rollbacks in progress, pausing eu-west batch. Updating status page and support thread.
maria: We'll keep this thread for rollout updates only. Post-rollback verification expected +20-40m. :thumbsup:
